name: PALESTINE
lead: Palestine sits at the crossroads of three continents, where ancient olive trees shade valleys seen by empires for thousands of years. From the West Bank hills to Gaza's coast, Palestinians are known for warm hospitality and poetry about home. Ramallah buzzes with cafés; Jerusalem draws pilgrims of three world religions.
geo: The West Bank rises in limestone hills of olive and almond groves, cut by wadis that rush with water after winter rain. The Jordan Valley drops to the Dead Sea shore — about 430 m below sea level, the lowest land on Earth.

Gaza Strip is a narrow Mediterranean ribbon, just 41 km long and 10 km wide, yet home to over two million people — one of the world's most densely populated places. Sandy beaches meet a flat, fertile coastal plain.
animals: Palestine sits on a great bird-migration highway. Storks, pelicans, eagles, and bee-eaters pour through every spring and autumn. The Palestine sunbird — a tiny gem with an iridescent green throat — is the national bird.

Gazelles still dart across the hillsides, and the Palestine mountain gazelle is named after this land. Striped hyenas, red foxes, and rock hyraxes — surprisingly distant cousins of elephants — hide in the rocky terrain.
culture: Palestinian cuisine is generous: maqluba (upside-down rice and vegetables), musakhan (chicken on flatbread with caramelised onions and sumac), and knafeh (hot cheese pastry in syrup) are beloved across the Arab world. Olive oil from ancient trees goes on nearly everything.

Embroidery called tatreez stitches vivid red geometric patterns onto dresses, telling stories of village and family. Dabke, a stomping line dance at weddings, brings everyone to their feet, and the oud (pear-shaped lute) fills evenings with music.
history: People farmed these hills since 9000 BCE. Canaanites, Egyptians, Greeks, Romans, and Crusaders each left marks. The name 'Palestine' echoes the ancient Philistines who lived along the coast. Jericho is considered the world's oldest city.

After Ottoman rule, Britain controlled the region from 1917. In 1948 Israel was declared and around 700,000 Palestinians fled — an event called the Nakba, meaning 'catastrophe'. Palestinians have sought an independent state ever since.
wows: Jericho is considered Earth's oldest city — people have lived there 11,000 years.
The Dead Sea is so salty you float like a cork — nearly 10x saltier than the ocean.
An olive tree near Bethlehem is estimated to be up to 5,000 years old and still fruiting.
The tiny Palestine sunbird hovers like a helicopter to sip nectar from flowers.
Tatreez stitch patterns are village-specific: experts read them like a postcode.
Nablus holds a knafeh festival drawing crowds for hot cheese-pastry in syrup.
The name 'Gaza' appears in Egyptian records 3,500 years old — one of history's oldest city names.

myths.fact: Jericho, in the West Bank, has walls and towers built 10,000 years ago — long before most civilisations existed anywhere on Earth.

myths.myth: The Dead Sea is actually a sea
myths.fact: It's a landlocked salt lake with no outlet — water only leaves by evaporation, making it grow saltier every year.
